title: Using survAHadjust
text: survAHadjust package calculates average hazard-based summaries adjusted survival curves. main workflow : adjusted survival curve methods, users can use adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv(). AIPTW, package provides aiptw_adjustedsurv().
code: adjusted survival curves   -> adjusted_ahsw()   -> ahsw_table()

title: Using survAHadjust
code: library(survAHadjust) library(survival)

title: Using survAHadjust
text: use pbc data survival package small example dataset.

what: Workflow 1: Analyze an existing adjusted survival curve object
title: Using survAHadjust
text: function adjusted_ahsw() accepts object contains adjusted survival curves adjsurv$adj. required columns : result can formatted using ahsw_table().
code: time surv group adjsurv_example <- list(   adj = data.frame(     time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),     group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),     surv = c(1.0, 0.80, 0.70, 1.0, 0.90, 0.85)   ) )  res_example <- adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv_example, to = 1, conf_int = FALSE)  res_example$est #>               group0    group1 difference     log_dif #> rmst       0.9000000 0.9500000  0.0500000  0.05406722 #> event_rate 0.3000000 0.1500000 -0.1500000 -0.69314718 #> ahsw       0.3333333 0.1578947 -0.1754386 -0.74721440 ahsw_table(res_example, method = "Example") #>    Method Group 0 AH Group 1 AH    DAH   RAH #> 1 Example      0.333      0.158 -0.175 0.474

title: Using survAHadjust
text: standard adjusted survival curve methods, users can first call adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() pass result adjusted_ahsw(). following code shows workflow. evaluated vignette depends adjustedCurves additional dependencies. methods adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() can used way, IPTW, matching, empirical likelihood, Kaplan-Meier methods.
code: D_ac <- D D_ac$Z <- factor(D_ac$Z)  outcome_model <- survival::coxph(   survival::Surv(Y, Delta) ~ Z + age + sex + bili + albumin,   data = D_ac,   x = TRUE )  adjsurv_direct <- adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv(   data = D_ac,   variable = "Z",   ev_time = "Y",   event = "Delta",   method = "direct",   outcome_model = outcome_model,   conf_int = FALSE,   bootstrap = FALSE )  res_direct <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv_direct,   to = 5,   conf_int = FALSE )  ahsw_table(res_direct, method = "Direct standardization")

title: Using survAHadjust
text: AIPTW standard doubly robust approach estimating adjusted survival curves. survAHadjust, function aiptw_adjustedsurv() implements AIPTW estimator used simulation study application. implementation follows AIPTW/IPCW setup described Ozenne et al. (2020). independent censoring, censoring distribution estimated using pooled Kaplan-Meier estimator; covars_cens supplied, Cox model used censoring distribution. non-AIPTW adjusted survival curve methods, users can use adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() pass resulting object adjusted_ahsw(). users prefer another implementation AIPTW returns adjusted survival curve object adj, time, surv, group, object can also passed adjusted_ahsw(). pass result adjusted_ahsw(). Format result:
code: adjsurv_aiptw <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = D,   covars_treat = c("age", "sex"),   covars_outcome = c("bili", "age", "albumin"),   y_col = "Y",   delta_col = "Delta",   z_col = "Z",   bootstrap = FALSE )  head(adjsurv_aiptw$adj) #>        time      surv group #> 1 0.0000000 1.0000000     0 #> 2 0.1122519 0.9944196     0 #> 3 0.1396304 0.9941534     0 #> 4 0.1943874 0.9876205     0 #> 5 0.2108145 0.9873209     0 #> 6 0.3011636 0.9870068     0 res_aiptw <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv_aiptw,   to = 5,   conf_int = FALSE )  res_aiptw$est #>                group0     group1   difference     log_dif #> rmst       4.31113377 4.17248530 -0.138648464 -0.03268907 #> event_rate 0.28738998 0.29232353  0.004933552  0.01702106 #> ahsw       0.06666227 0.07005981  0.003397537  0.04971014 ahsw_table(res_aiptw, method = "AIPTW") #>   Method Group 0 AH Group 1 AH   DAH   RAH #> 1  AIPTW      0.067      0.070 0.003 1.051

title: Using survAHadjust
text: Bootstrap inference can requested setting bootstrap = TRUE. real analyses, use larger number bootstrap samples, n_boot = 300. following code evaluated vignette can take longer run. example shows workflow real analyses. small example evaluated show structure bootstrap output confidence interval level appears output column names. conf_level = 0.90, confidence interval columns named low_90 high_90. Similarly, conf_level = 0.95, columns named low_95 high_95. helper function ahsw_table() uses confidence interval column names label summary table.
code: adjsurv_aiptw_boot <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = D,   covars_treat = c("age", "sex"),   covars_outcome = c("bili", "age", "albumin"),   y_col = "Y",   delta_col = "Delta",   z_col = "Z",   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 300 )  res_aiptw_boot <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv_aiptw_boot,   to = 5,   conf_int = TRUE )  ahsw_table(res_aiptw_boot, method = "AIPTW") adjsurv_boot_example <- list(   adj = data.frame(     time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),     group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),     surv = c(1.0, 0.80, 0.70, 1.0, 0.90, 0.85)   ),   boot_data = rbind(     data.frame(       time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),       group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),       surv = c(1.0, 0.82, 0.72, 1.0, 0.91, 0.86),       boot = 1     ),     data.frame(       time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),       group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),       surv = c(1.0, 0.78, 0.68, 1.0, 0.89, 0.84),       boot = 2     )   ) )  res_boot_90 <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv_boot_example,   to = 1,   conf_int = TRUE,   conf_level = 0.90 )  res_boot_90$ahsw #>                   est          se     low_90    high_90 p_value #> group0      0.3333333 0.036669323  0.2730177  0.3936490      NA #> group1      0.1578947 0.016062150  0.1314749  0.1843146      NA #> difference -0.1754386 0.020607173 -0.2093344 -0.1415428       0 #> log_dif    -0.7472144 0.008270833 -0.7608187 -0.7336101       0 ahsw_table(res_boot_90, method = "Example") #>    Method    Group 0 AH (90% CI)    Group 1 AH (90% CI) #> 1 Example 0.333 (0.273 to 0.394) 0.158 (0.131 to 0.184) #>                DAH (90% CI)           RAH (90% CI) #> 1 -0.175 (-0.209 to -0.142) 0.474 (0.467 to 0.480)

title: Using survAHadjust
text: Results multiple methods can combined rbind(). following code shows combine results standard methods AIPTW. evaluated vignette res_direct created non-evaluated example . evaluated example vignette, show AIPTW row.
code: tab_all <- rbind(   ahsw_table(res_direct, method = "Direct standardization"),   ahsw_table(res_aiptw, method = "AIPTW") )  tab_all tab_aiptw <- rbind(   ahsw_table(res_aiptw, method = "AIPTW") )  tab_aiptw #>   Method Group 0 AH Group 1 AH   DAH   RAH #> 1  AIPTW      0.067      0.070 0.003 1.051

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight
text: adjusted_ahsw() requires adjusted survival curve object : result can formatted one-row table:
code: adjsurv$adj$time adjsurv$adj$surv adjsurv$adj$group library(survAHadjust)  adjsurv <- list(   adj = data.frame(     time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),     group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),     surv = c(1.0, 0.80, 0.70, 1.0, 0.90, 0.85)   ) )  res <- adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv, to = 1, conf_int = FALSE)  res$est #>               group0    group1 difference     log_dif #> rmst       0.9000000 0.9500000  0.0500000  0.05406722 #> event_rate 0.3000000 0.1500000 -0.1500000 -0.69314718 #> ahsw       0.3333333 0.1578947 -0.1754386 -0.74721440 ahsw_table(res, method = "Example") #>    Method Group 0 AH Group 1 AH    DAH   RAH #> 1 Example      0.333      0.158 -0.175 0.474

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight
text: standard adjusted survival curve methods, use adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() first. example: methods adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() can used way.
code: outcome_model <- survival::coxph(   survival::Surv(time, event) ~ group + x1 + x2 + x3,   data = dat,   x = TRUE )  adjsurv <- adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv(   data = dat,   variable = "group",   ev_time = "time",   event = "event",   method = "direct",   outcome_model = outcome_model,   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 300 )  res <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv,   to = 0.7,   conf_int = TRUE )  ahsw_table(res, method = "Direct standardization")

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight
text: AIPTW standard doubly robust approach estimating adjusted survival curves. survAHadjust, function aiptw_adjustedsurv() implements AIPTW estimator used simulation study application. implementation follows AIPTW/IPCW setup described Ozenne et al. (2020). independent censoring, censoring distribution estimated using pooled Kaplan-Meier estimator; covars_cens supplied, Cox model used censoring distribution. non-AIPTW adjusted survival curve methods, users can use adjustedCurves::adjustedsurv() pass resulting object adjusted_ahsw(). users prefer another implementation AIPTW returns adjusted survival curve object adj, time, surv, group, object can also passed adjusted_ahsw(). censoring depends covariates, specify covars_cens:
code: adjsurv_aiptw <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = dat,   covars_treat = c("x2", "x3", "x5", "x6"),   covars_outcome = c("x1", "x2", "x4", "x5_squared"),   covars_cens = NULL,   y_col = "time",   delta_col = "event",   z_col = "group",   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 300 )  res_aiptw <- adjusted_ahsw(   adjsurv = adjsurv_aiptw,   to = 0.7,   conf_int = TRUE )  ahsw_table(res_aiptw, method = "AIPTW") adjsurv_aiptw <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = dat,   covars_treat = c("x2", "x3", "x5", "x6"),   covars_outcome = c("x1", "x2", "x4", "x5_squared"),   covars_cens = c("x2"),   y_col = "time",   delta_col = "event",   z_col = "group",   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 300 )

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight
text: adjusted_ahsw() always returns point estimates : object res$est contains RMST, event rate, AHSW: , difference : log_dif : AHSW row, exp(log_dif) gives ratio average hazards. conf_int = TRUE bootstrap data available, adjusted_ahsw() also returns bootstrap-based inference tables: tables give inference results RMST, event rate, AHSW, respectively. table rows: columns: , XX determined user-specified conf_level. example, conf_level = 0.95, confidence interval columns : conf_level = 0.90, confidence interval columns : p_value reported difference log_dif. p-values group0 group1 set NA, main comparisons difference ratio groups. example, res$ahsw gives bootstrap-based inference AHSW. log_dif row log ratio average hazards. conf_level = 0.95, ratio confidence interval can obtained exponentiating log-scale values: different confidence level used, replace low_95 high_95 corresponding column names. helper function ahsw_table() uses confidence interval column names label summary table. example, bootstrap inference table contains low_95 high_95, formatted table use column names Group 0 AH (95% CI), Group 1 AH (95% CI), DAH (95% CI), RAH (95% CI).
code: res$est group0  group1  difference  log_dif rmst event_rate ahsw group1 - group0 log(group1) - log(group0) res$rmst res$evrt res$ahsw group0 group1 difference log_dif est       point estimate se        bootstrap standard error low_XX    lower confidence limit high_XX   upper confidence limit p_value   two-sided p-value low_95 high_95 low_90 high_90 exp(res$ahsw["log_dif", c("est", "low_95", "high_95")])

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight (AHSW) — adjusted_ahsw
code: adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv, to, from=0, conf_int=FALSE, conf_level=0.95)

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight (AHSW) — adjusted_ahsw
text: adjsurv list object resulting adjusted survival analysis containing survival probabilities (adjsurv$adj) optionally bootstrap data (adjsurv$boot_data). Numeric. upper time limit (tau) calculating RMST AHSW. Numeric. Lower time limit integration (default 0). conf_int Logical. TRUE, calculates bootstrap-based confidence intervals. conf_level Numeric. Confidence level intervals (default 0.95).

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight (AHSW) — adjusted_ahsw
text: list containing: est data frame point estimates RMST, event rate, AHSW two groups, difference, log difference. rmst data frame bootstrap-based estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, p-values RMST. Confidence interval columns named according conf_level, example low_95 high_95 conf_level = 0.95. evrt Similar results rmst event rate. ahsw Similar results rmst AHSW.

title: Adjusted Average Hazard with Survival Weight (AHSW) — adjusted_ahsw
text: also calculates confidence intervals p-values using bootstrapped standard errors.

what: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
title: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
text: Format output adjusted_ahsw() one-row summary table. useful making paper-style tables group-specific AH, AH difference, AH ratio.

title: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
code: ahsw_table(   x,   method = NULL,   group0_name = "Group 0",   group1_name = "Group 1",   digits = 3 )

title: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
text: x Output adjusted_ahsw(). method Character string method name. group0_name Column name group 0. group1_name Column name group 1. digits Number digits display.

title: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
text: one-row data frame. bootstrap-based inference available, confidence interval levels shown column names, example Group 0 AH (95% CI) RAH (95% CI).

title: Create a summary table for adjusted average hazard results — ahsw_table
code: adjsurv <- list(   adj = data.frame(     time = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0),     group = factor(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)),     surv = c(1.0, 0.80, 0.70, 1.0, 0.90, 0.85)   ) )  res <- adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv, to = 1, conf_int = FALSE) ahsw_table(res, method = "Example") #>    Method Group 0 AH Group 1 AH    DAH   RAH #> 1 Example      0.333      0.158 -0.175 0.474

what: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
text: Estimates adjusted survival curves using augmented inverse probability treatment weighting (AIPTW). implementation follows AIPTW/IPCW setup used simulation study application.

title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
code: aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data,   covars_treat,   covars_outcome,   covars_cens = NULL,   y_col = "time",   delta_col = "event",   z_col = "group",   bootstrap = FALSE,   n_boot = 300,   ps_clip = c(1e-06, 1 - 1e-06),   g_clip = 1e-06 )

title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
text: data data frame. covars_treat Character vector covariates treatment model. covars_outcome Character vector covariates outcome model. covars_cens Character vector covariates censoring model. NULL, pooled KM used censoring. NULL, Cox model used censoring. y_col Name observed time variable. Default "time". delta_col Name event indicator variable. Default "event". z_col Name treatment/group variable. variable coded 0/1. Default "group". bootstrap Logical. TRUE, bootstrap adjusted survival curves generated stored boot_data. n_boot Number bootstrap samples. ps_clip Truncation range propensity scores. g_clip Lower bound censoring survival probabilities.

title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
text: adjusted survival curve object. main element adj, data frame columns time, surv, group. bootstrap = TRUE, object also contains boot_data.

title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
text: Ozenne B, Scheike TH, Staerk L, Gerds TA. estimation average treatment effects right-censored time event outcome competing risks. Biometrical Journal. 2020;62(3):751-763.

title: Estimate adjusted survival curves using AIPTW — aiptw_adjustedsurv
code: D <- survival::pbc[!is.na(survival::pbc$trt), ] D$Y <- D$time / 365.25 D$Delta <- as.numeric(D$status == 2) D$Z <- as.numeric(D$trt == 2)  D <- D[complete.cases(D[, c("Y", "Delta", "Z", "age", "sex", "bili", "albumin")]), ]  adjsurv <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = D,   covars_treat = c("age", "sex"),   covars_outcome = c("bili", "age", "albumin"),   y_col = "Y",   delta_col = "Delta",   z_col = "Z",   bootstrap = FALSE )  adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv, to = 5, conf_int = FALSE) #> $est #>                group0     group1   difference     log_dif #> rmst       4.31113377 4.17248530 -0.138648464 -0.03268907 #> event_rate 0.28738998 0.29232353  0.004933552  0.01702106 #> ahsw       0.06666227 0.07005981  0.003397537  0.04971014 #>   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ adjsurv_boot <- aiptw_adjustedsurv(   data = D,   covars_treat = c("age", "sex"),   covars_outcome = c("bili", "age", "albumin"),   y_col = "Y",   delta_col = "Delta",   z_col = "Z",   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 300 )  adjusted_ahsw(adjsurv_boot, to = 5, conf_int = TRUE) } # }
